title: Crash-prompt toggle persists to PreferencesStore but boot reads DevicePreferencesStore — choice may not survive relaunch

description: Discovered during plan-1d (export-schema-completeness) while researching the exclusion rationale for AppPreferences' Plan-21 device-local fields — not one of the 70 findings in the 2026-07-28 review, and NOT fixed as part of 1d (out of scope; flagged instead). Trail: CrashReportingSection (Apps/Lillist-iOS/Sources/Settings/CrashReportingSection.swift, embedded via DebugPage.swift) and CrashReportingPane (Apps/Lillist-macOS/Sources/Preferences/CrashReportingPane.swift) both bind PreferencesStore.Prefs.crashPromptsEnabled (Core-Data-backed AppPreferences row) for the Settings toggle. SettingsTab.swift (iOS) persists the WHOLE Prefs struct back via preferencesStore.update on change, so the Core Data column IS live-written by this toggle. But AppEnvironment.crashPromptsEnabled -- the value CrashReporterHost actually reads at boot (AppEnvironment.swift line ~553: self.crashPromptsEnabled = await devicePreferences.crashPromptsEnabled()) -- initializes from DevicePreferencesStore (App Group UserDefaults), the Plan-21 partitioned store. The toggle's .onChange handler only mirrors the new value into the in-memory environment.crashPromptsEnabled; it never calls devicePreferences.setCrashPromptsEnabled. Net effect: a user's crash-prompt choice, made via Settings, updates the Core Data row (which AppPreferencesPartitionMigrator's doc comment says is legacy/device-partition scaffolding, not the source of truth) but never updates DevicePreferencesStore (the actual boot-time source of truth) -- so the choice may silently revert to whatever DevicePreferencesStore last held on the next relaunch. Reproduce: toggle crash prompts off in Settings, force-quit, relaunch, check whether the prompt still fires. Fix likely needs the toggle to call devicePreferences.setCrashPromptsEnabled directly (or route entirely off PreferencesStore.Prefs for this one field) -- same preferences-partition territory as 5a's PreferencesStore.read() findings, hence plan-6a rather than bloating 3a/5a. Full discovery context: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-28-plan-1d-export-schema-completeness.md and the ledger's Wave 1d closing report / Current Status flag.
